reasons: The finding is claimed compliant and correctly proposes no redline and no counterparty comment, which is the expected output for a compliant classification.

Section 10(a) is a genuine Vendor-side defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and Kubient's (and its subcontractors') acts or omissions — broad enough to reach third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Services, especially read with the cited non-infringement, data-security and compliance-with-law warranties.

Section 11 supplies the standard indemnification procedure the rule expects (notice not a condition to recovery, indemnitor control of defence, no settlement admitting indemnitee liability without consent, cooperation at indemnitor's cost), and the rationale notes no sub-cap applies.

The failed deterministic check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a keyword heuristic; the indemnity does not exclude IP infringement, it simply covers it through broad 'arising out of the Services / breach of warranty' language, so the heuristic miss does not undermine the classification.

The Customer-side indemnity at 10(b) is a mirror limited to Customer Content/Properties, misuse and Customer breach; the slightly wider 'acts or omissions of Customer' limb and the 'best of its knowledge' qualifier on the Creative limb are properly noted in the rationale as minor sub-elements rather than flagged as deviations.
